title: Hate
author: potatobill_IV
selftext:
How do y'all deal with the hate of using AI to make games.

I have awesome story lines and vision but no coding experience. Also no one who I know can code, or feels as passionate about the games as I do until I make them.

comments.author: cowman3456
comments.body: Mainly by losing faith in humanity.

comments.author: orellanaed
comments.body: Ignore them. As long as you put in thought, effort and care into your game (and make it fun to play), gamers won't care.

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body:
People are hating everywhere - even here in this sub

Just ignore and keep building

comments.author: xexpanderx
comments.body:
Just dont give a fuck about them. We live in a new era, and a lot of people seems to have big time of acceptance. Just ignore them. Their biggest argument is that the quality of the AI code is bad, they may be right, but what they dont realize is that this will get better with time. What will they complain about then?

I just love that AI can create something based on my idea and design, how nice is not that?

comments.author: Inbellator
comments.body: make something so good with ai that people have to question their own ideas about using it.

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body: At the moment big gaming subs/spaces are looking at AI doing stuff like PC ports of old and latest games and starting to come around. And there's little hate, people are just like "oh shit that's cool" so give it time I reckon lol :)

comments.author: guillermosan
comments.body: Ignore it. It won't last long in any case. If you have an idea and a desire to materialize it, go for it. Its incredibly fun, even if you don't make a great game, its worth it.

comments.author: Radiant-Mountain-257
comments.body: Hate is just part of this job with our without AI.

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
You need to be open to suggestion, but first filter trough what's the intention of people saying it.

Most of them is just basicly ignore category.  
As someone that earn money on internet hater always exist.  
I earn money on writing novel, even before ai era,  someone cursing even treaten to kill me is nothing new. 

This happen even on big platform like kindle, that have moderation etc.

comments.author: francoperdu
comments.body: It can really suck. My best friend was a jerk about my ai game when I showed him. He's still my bro. Haters gonna hate, I guess

comments.author: YesterdayOptimal3552
comments.body: someday, with AI, we will be able to make things with exactly the same results without AI, but much faster. If not so we have to study more about AI or the target field

comments.author: Global_Wing9181
comments.body: Get over it.  If you don't use AI to code, it will never compare or keep up with the ones that do. By a long shot.

comments.author: Regular-Dingo-2872
comments.body: you ignore it completely and when you hit something really good that people want to play it doesnt matter

comments.author: StretchedNut
comments.body: I’ve been a dev since before AI. There were haters then too, so I just do what I always do and carry on

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
Hate from whom? Mentally ill people on reddit? Lol

If I get 10 positive and one negative response, why would I bother with the negative response. Don't produce trash and people will love your stuff

comments.author: loxagos_snake
comments.body:
No one who actively works on game projects 'hates' anyone who uses AI to make games.

But some of us choose to hold a balanced perspective when it comes to what AI can or can't do, because we also use it in a professional capacity. In essence, AI reproducing a cookie-cutter game with a single prompt is certainly a sign of galloping progress, but does not mean I have to agree with someone who confidently claims that a single beginner developer can make GTA VI with a few prompts.

That's about the AI assistance/programming part. When it comes to AI-generated assets, it's a whole different discussion. It stands on shaky ethical grounds, but even if you ignore that, it looks generic and characteristically artificial.

My general position is that no amount of AI assistance is going to replace actually knowing what you're doing, so it pays to make an effort to learn. It's the difference between pulling the lever on a slot machine and praying that it gets it right this time (burning money in the process), and knowingly leveraging a powerful tool to shape your vision.

In the end, if you want to make a game using AI, you don't have to listen to what anyone online says. People often 'hate' others because they have nothing better to do with their time. That doesn't mean there are no merits to the arguments *against* its use.
